title: Rav Chisda ben Avira
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is cited in [Yalkut Shmuel, remez 118](https://www.sefaria.org/Yalkut_Shimoni_on_Nach.118.2), as saying: “Tasting does not count as eating,” etc.[^1] Hyman traces the saying to Yerushalmi Nedarim, at the beginning of chapter 1, where it reads R' Ba Chasida in the name of R' Zeira. Without doubt, he argues, a conflation involving Zeira produced Avira, and R' Ba Chasida became Rav Chisda. Midrash Shmuel likewise gives “R' Ba Chasida bar R' Zeira.” Hyman explains ב״ר here as an abbreviation for בשם ר׳, “in the name of R'.”[^2][^3]

notes.text: The accepted Hebrew has the Yalkut locator קה (105); the targeted native page instead appears to read קח (108), while the older machine text had קיח (118). The matching full saying is present at remez 118 in the checked digital Yalkut Shimoni on Nach, including the name רב חסדא בן אעוירא. The English links that checked locus rather than silently retaining an unrelated modern 105 or 108. This does not establish which historical numbering Hyman intended. His own heading עוירא is preserved as Avira; the extra aleph in the retrieved Yalkut spelling is not silently substituted.

The earlier “a woman who tastes” was too narrow. The matching Midrash Shmuel 17:3 passage, in the Krakow 1893 text, discusses Jonathan tasting honey and then quotes המטעומת אין בה לא משום אכילה. Rashi’s Vilna commentary on Berakhot 14a:8 explicitly glosses מטעמת as טעימת תבשיל, tasting a cooked dish. “Tasting does not count as eating” conveys the legal category without inventing a female participant. The omitted continuation is marked by Hyman’s own “etc.”

The accepted final transcription reads וזעירא הוא ר״ת ב״ר כשם ר׳. The targeted native page instead reads זעירא והוא ר״ת ב״ר בשם ר׳, directly after ר׳ בא חסידא בר ר׳. This makes the complete name and Hyman’s abbreviation explanation intelligible: he takes ב״ר as short for בשם ר׳, “in the name of R',” rather than using it to establish a father-son relationship. The checked Midrash Shmuel paragraph contains ר׳ בא חסידא בר ר׳ זעירא. Its titles are abbreviated, so they remain R'. Hyman’s confident conflation claim is translated with “without doubt” but remains his claim, not an identity binding. The stated Yerushalmi Nedarim source was not located in the checked opening section; no alternative tractate or locator is substituted. The accepted Hebrew remains unchanged.
